content:
anya: Proposal: introduce segmented headroom multipliers + burst gating per reserved pool segment (enterprise/scale/experimental). idea is to let enterprise pools keep higher headroom for SLOs while scale pools use tighter multipliers to optimize utilization.

mike: high-level sounds good. do we have a metric set to measure customer impact? latency P99, throttle rate, and outage incidents?

anya: yes — target metrics: token latency P99, request rejections (throttle), and burst spillover rate. also want per-tenant cost delta. we should define thresholds for auto-rollbacks.

keiko: operational concerns: segmented multipliers mean more tuning knobs. how do oncall and autoscaler interact?

anya: plan: autoscaler respects segment multiplier as a soft headroom target. we add a grace window for scale-down to avoid thrash. default grace = 10m, configurable per pool.

sam: +1 on grace window. also suggest an emergency preemption floor for enterprise so bursts never drop below X qps during recovery.

darren: customer ask from Lighthouse: they want guaranteed burst carryover for certain windows. this intersects with multipliers. can we add a per-contract override?

anya: yes — propose a per-contract soft-override flag: "carryover_allowed": true/false and a max_carryover_seconds. enforced by admission layer, not autoscaler.

mike: rollout plan? we need a canary on a few pools, telemetry dashboards, and a kill-switch.

anya: rollout steps: 1) feature flag behind config service; 2) canary on internal test tenant + 2 low-risk customer pools; 3) 2-week telemetry collection; 4) expand to >50% of pools; 5) GA. kill-switch via config toggle.

keiko: launch criteria suggestion: no >2% increase in P99 latency across canary pools, rejections under 0.5% of baseline, and no oncall pages for admission failures for 14 days.

sam: add checks for billing delta — customers should have visibility before we flip GA. create a per-customer impact report.

anya: agreed — will add a cost-impact exporter. also need API for customers to opt into/off segmented multiplier per contract.

darren: scope negotiation: we probably can't do per-tenant UI before GA. API-only for pilot customers, UI later.

mike: technical: admission layer needs to compute effective multiplier = max(segment_multiplier, contract_override_multiplier) and then gate. pseudocode: 

```
// compute effective headroom
segment = lookup_segment(pool_id)
segment_mul = config.segment_multipliers[segment]
contract_mul = contract.override_multiplier || 0
effective = Math.max(segment_mul, contract_mul)
if (request_exceeds_capacity * effective) -> route via burst-gate -> allow/queue/preempt
```

keiko: logging + tracing: annotate admission decisions with segment, effective multiplier, and reason. important for root cause.

anya: testing: we need unit tests for computation, simulation harness for 10k qps burst shapes, and a chaos test that toggles overrides during peak.

oncall-bot: Reminder: add oncall runbook entries for new failure modes (admission misclassify, override drift).

sam: timeline ask: can we get a working pilot in 6 weeks?

anya: target 6–8 weeks. I'll draft a short RFC and ship a feature-flagged PR. volunteers for code review: @mike @keiko.

mike: happy to review.

keiko: will take ops review and runbook updates.

anya: thanks — I'll post the RFC in #product and link to this thread. if no objections by EOD Friday, we start sprint planning.
